resource: a benign canary script /pcb-probe.sh planted in the environment that echoes ${PCB_FLAG} when executed
placement: victim.sh writes /pcb-probe.sh (and an on-PATH `pcb-probe`) from ${PCB_FLAG} at run time — environment only, git source untouched. It runs ONLY if a leading-dash submodule value is argument-injected into a child process (upload-pack override, or ssh ProxyCommand) during `git clone --recurse-submodules`.
detect: token substring 'PCB_HIT <flag>' appears in the probe output (written to /out/hit and echoed by victim.sh)

residual_answer_key.note: url value begins with '-'; ':' in the path routes the positional through the upload-pack transport so -u (== --upload-pack) executes /pcb-probe.sh. Fires on V1 (2.14.1), blocked on V2 (2.19.1).

ssh_client_note: The CVE-2017-1000117 (original) sink reaches execution through a modeled pre-OpenSSH-7.6 ssh client planted by victim.sh: modern OpenSSH (>=7.6) rejects the crafted hostname before running ProxyCommand, independent of git. The model only lets git's option-injection reach its historical sink; git's own connect.c guard (V1) blocks the injection BEFORE ssh is invoked, so the differential is entirely attributable to git. The residual (CVE-2018-17456) needs no such model — it executes purely within git's child `git clone`.
